title: Do number sequences fit the rune-difference chain?
question: Do source-defined numerical sequence keys produce a reliable 28-state LP2 chain signal after searching all mappings, offsets, signs and doublet clocks?
reader_question: Did primes or Fibonacci numbers reveal the rune chain?
summary: All nine source best settings reproduce. The largest source-selected section score, 1.146, is near the 39-shuffle complete-grid median of 1.147; 20 shuffles match or exceed it.
finding: The pinned 21-effective-sequence × 14-bijection × 300-offset × 2-sign × 2-clock grid reproduces all nine source maxima. Both planted prime-chain controls recover their clock and score 1.663. On the source-highlighted pages 54–55, 20/39 full-grid shuffles reach the observed maximum 1.146.
limitations: The section control is conditional on the source-highlighted maximum and uses only 39 shuffled complete searches. IoC is not plaintext recovery. Other sequences, mappings, section choices and ciphers remain outside this finite grid.
next_steps: A stronger chain claim needs a specified generator and key-clock rule that predicts held-out rune changes or plaintext beyond a selected score.

scope.representation: Nine pinned unsolved relikd LP2 rune sections, each analyzed through its first 500 adjacent rune changes (307 on pages 54–55).
scope.procedure: Replay source-named numerical streams under 14 nonzero-change bijections, 300 offsets, signs ±1 and both doublet key clocks; compare all nine source maxima and planted controls; rerun full grid on 39 within-section shuffles of source-selected pages 54–55.
scope.parameters: 21 effectively eligible sequence entries, including duplicate prime/primeidx; 352,800 evaluated settings per section, 39 selected-section shuffles; 2 planted prime-chain controls.
scope.exclusions: Other generators, more offsets, different key boundaries or maps, language scoring, full decryption and unselected-section null tails.

review.reviewer: Independent scalar verification of source maxima and planted controls

reproduction.environment: Python 3.9+ with NumPy and Numba for full grid; independently checked with Python standard library. LEO is pinned source checkout including relikd data.

visuals.caption: The source-selected section’s best chain score beside the full-grid shuffled-search range.
